title: Find Missing Constants by Fitting Equivalent Expressions
description: Find missing constants in equivalent expressions by defining comparison inputs, fitting with Desmos, checking the match, and reading the requested quantity.

questions.stem_html: The identity \((x+4)(x+8)=x^{2}+32+kx\) holds for every real x. What is \(k\)?
questions.explanation_html: Use a list of distinct x-values on both sides and fit the unknown coefficients. The product is \(x^{2}+12x+32\), so the requested value is 12. Verify the match across the full list.
questions.variation: Find one missing constant in an identity

questions.stem_html: The identity \((2x+3)(5x+4)=10x^2+bx+c\) holds for every real x. What is \(b+c\)?
questions.explanation_html: Use a list of distinct x-values on both sides and fit the unknown coefficients. The product is \(10x^{2}+23x+12\), so the requested value is 35. Verify the match across the full list.
questions.variation: Fit two constants and report a requested combination

questions.stem_html: The identity \((2x+7)(2x+5)=ax^2+bx+c\) holds for every real x. What is \(a+b+c\)?
questions.explanation_html: Use a list of distinct x-values on both sides and fit the unknown coefficients. The product is \(4x^{2}+24x+35\), so the requested value is 63. Verify the match across the full list.
questions.variation: Use enough distinct inputs for three unknown coefficients

questions.stem_html: For every real x except \(x=-6\), the identity \(\frac{x^2-36}{x+6}=1x+k\) holds. What is k?
questions.explanation_html: Fit values such as 0 and 1 that keep the denominator nonzero, then verify the identity by cancellation. The quotient is \(x-6\), so with coefficient 1, the constant is -6.
questions.variation: Fit a rational identity on its allowed domain

questions.explanation_html: Fit u, v, and w with at least four distinct t-values and check that the fit stays stable. Expansion gives \(2t^{2}+12t+22\); subtracting the constant from the linear coefficient gives -10.
questions.variation: Fit in another input letter and compute a derived value
